items.title: Mike Brown On Struggling Knicks: 'We Have To Hit Singles'
items.summary: New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown said that his team has to return to playing simple after a 98-93 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday night. They are now 2-4 on the season. "We're trying to get a home run every time we get the ball," Brown said. "We have to hit singles." The Knicks shot just 40.7% from the field and 31.7% from three. Jalen Brunson added that the Knicks need to be more decisive in their play. "Sometimes it can be us being hesitant as well, wanting to make the right play," said Brunson. "We understand what we have to do, it's just starting the game that way. That has to be our biggest point of emphasis going forward." Mikel Bridges continued his early season struggles, finishing with 12 points and five rebounds. Bridges is averaging 6.2 points and 2.8 rebounds on the year. Karl-Anthony Towns echoed Brunson in saying that the team needs to improve how they start games. "I think we did a great job in the fourth quarter of finding that gear, of getting out the quicksand, finally turning gears into motion. "It puts us in position where you've got to make some magic happen, and we just didn't have enough magic today to get back and win the game," said Towns.

items.title: LeBron James, Joel Embiid Out Saturday Due To Injury Management
items.summary: LeBron James and Joel Embiid will miss the Philadelphia 76ers' matchup against the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday due to injury management. James will miss the game due to low back/sciatica, with Embiid out with right foot plantar fasciitis. The Hornets game is a back-to-back for the Sixers, with the team expected to be cautious with James and Embiid throughout the season. James finished with what Nick Nurse called his " best game " for the Sixers on Friday night against the Knicks.

items.title: LeBron James Has 'Best Game' For Sixers In Win Over Knicks
items.summary: LeBron James finished with 20 points, nine rebounds, and eight assists in the Philadelphia 76ers' 98-93 win over the New York Knicks in the NBA Cup on Friday night. "He's been good, but that was his best game for sure," Philly coach Nick Nurse said of James. Tyrese Maxey described James as a "calming presence" in late-game situations, with the Sixers winning all five of their games in clutch time. "At the end of the day, he's LeBron James," Maxey said. "So it's just like he can do stuff like he did tonight, a couple of big buckets." James also tied Kareem Abdul-Jabbar as the fifth-oldest in NBA history to score 20 points. The Sixers were without Jaylen Brown, who sat the game with a left patellar injury. James added that he was enjoying his time in Philadelphia. "I'm having a great time," James said. "... I'm a big-ass kid, to be completely honest, but these guys are great to be around, and I'm more than happy that I've made the decision to come here."
